introduction: Today, fifty days after Easter, we celebrate Pentecost. The Holy Spirit comes upon the disciples like a mighty wind and tongues of fire, and they proclaim the mighty works of God in every language. Jesus promised that the Spirit of truth would guide his Church into all truth. Paul names the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace. With Pentecost the Easter season ends. Let us pray: Come, Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Spirit of God renews the face of the earth. Let us bring our prayers to the Father, in the power of the Spirit.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world: that the Holy Spirit may renew her and make her a witness to the mighty works of God in every language. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who were confirmed this year: that they may use the gifts of the Spirit for the good of others. Let us pray to the Lord.
For a world divided by language, nation and hatred: that the Spirit may bring understanding, peace and unity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are sad, anxious or without hope: that the Spirit may fill them with love, joy and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may walk by the Spirit and bear his fruit in our homes and workplaces. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you sent your Holy Spirit on the Church at Pentecost. Pour out his gifts on us again, and make us faithful witnesses to your Son in all the world. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Walk by the Spirit
reflection.body:
Pentecost was already a Jewish feast, fifty days after Passover, which brought pilgrims to Jerusalem from many lands. On that day, Luke tells us, the disciples "were all with one accord in one place." Suddenly there came "a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind," and "Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them." They "were all filled with the Holy Spirit."

The crowd that gathers is amazed. These are ordinary Galileans, yet everyone hears them in his own language: "we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!" At Babel, human pride scattered the nations by confusing their speech. At Pentecost, the Church has long seen the reverse: the Spirit gathers the nations into one people of God, without erasing their differences.

In the Gospel, Jesus promises the Spirit as a guide: "when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth." The Spirit does not bring a new Gospel. "He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine and will declare it to you." He helps the Church understand and live what Jesus gave her.

Paul tells us how to recognize the Spirit's work in a life. He contrasts the works of the flesh with something else: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control." And he concludes: "If we live by the Spirit, let's also walk by the Spirit."

The psalm prays for every age: "You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground." Today the Easter season ends, but the Spirit's work in us is only beginning. This week, choose one fruit of the Spirit from Paul's list, the one you most need, and ask for it every morning.
